definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese end-blown bamboo flute, known for its meditative, breathy tone.

examples.japanese: {尺八|しゃくはち}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{吹|ふ}く→吹く：02445_fuku⟧。
{尺八|しゃくはち}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{音色|ねいろ}→音色：07422_neiro⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{心|こころ}→心：01321_kokoro⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{落|お}ち{着|つ}く→落ち着く：04670_ochitsuku⟧。
examples.english: The sound of the shakuhachi is calming.

notes:
NAME ORIGIN: {尺八|しゃくはち} literally means "one shaku and eight sun" (approximately 54.5 cm), the standard length of the instrument.

CHARACTERISTICS:
- Made of madake bamboo (⟦{真竹|まだけ}→真竹：noentry⟧)
- End-blown (not side-blown like Western flutes)
- Five finger holes (4 front, 1 back)
- Breathy, meditative tone

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {尺八|しゃくはち}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{吹|ふ}く→吹く：02445_fuku⟧ (to play shakuhachi)
- {尺八|しゃくはち}⟦{奏者|そうしゃ}→奏者：06964_sousha⟧ (shakuhachi player)
- ⟦{本曲|ほんきょく}→本曲：noentry⟧ (solo shakuhachi pieces)

ETYMOLOGY:
Originally associated with ⟦{虚無僧|こむそう}→虚無僧：28512_komusou⟧ (Fuke Zen Buddhist monks) who played shakuhachi as a form of meditation (⟦{吹禅|すいぜん}→吹禅：noentry⟧).

GENRES:
- ⟦{邦楽|ほうがく}→邦楽：14456_hougaku⟧ (traditional Japanese music)
- ⟦{三曲|さんきょく}→三曲：noentry⟧ (ensemble with koto and shamisen)
